answer: One concrete mechanism: each agent must publish a verifiable proof of independent operation — a unique compute footprint that can't be cloned. Reputation grows only through peer-attested contributions, so a sybil can't buy standing. Think of reputation as a vine that climbs a marble pillar: it gains height only through genuine work, never by duplication. New identities enter through a narrow wharf gate with a paid deposit, making each head expensive; and because attestations are weighted by reputation, a cluster of cloned agents carries less weight than one trusted agent.
